title: Minimum Genetic Mutation
hints: this is a shortest-path problem in disguise - what are the 'nodes' and what connects two nodes with an edge?
two genes are connected by an edge if they differ in exactly one character position, and the destination gene must be in the bank
BFS naturally finds the shortest number of edges (mutations) between a start node and a target node - what would you enqueue first?
start a BFS from startGene, and at each gene try all L positions times 4 letters as candidate mutations, only enqueueing ones that are in the bank and haven't been visited yet
track the number of mutations as the BFS depth, and return it as soon as you dequeue endGene; if the queue empties first, return -1
commonMistakes: requiring startGene itself to be present in the bank, when only intermediate and final genes along the path need to be
using DFS without tracking the minimum across all paths, which can return a longer path than necessary
not marking genes as visited, causing infinite loops or redundant re-exploration in the BFS
forgetting to check that endGene is actually reachable/in the bank before or during the search, and returning 0 or an incorrect fallback instead of -1

content.problemStatement:
A gene string is represented as an 8-character string made only of the
letters A, C, G, and T. A single mutation changes exactly one character
in the gene string to a different one of those four letters. You're given
a starting gene `startGene`, a target gene `endGene`, and a `bank` of
valid intermediate genes (a single space-delimited string). Every gene
that appears along the path from `startGene` to `endGene`, except
`startGene` itself, must be present in the bank.

**Return the minimum number of mutations needed to transform `startGene` into `endGene`, changing one character per mutation and passing only through genes in the bank, or -1 if there's no such sequence of mutations.**

`startGene` itself is not required to be in the bank.
constraints: startGene, endGene, and every gene in bank consist only of the characters A, C, G, T
notes: endGene is not present in the bank at all (impossible, return -1)
a valid path exists but requires passing through several intermediate mutations
startGene already differs from endGene by exactly one character and that one mutation lands directly in the bank

sampleTestCases.explanation: changing the last character T to A directly reaches endGene, and AACCGGTA is in the bank
AACCGGTT -> AACCGGTA -> AAACGGTA, two mutations, both intermediate/final genes are in the bank
AAAAACCC -> AAAACCCC -> AAACCCCC -> AACCCCCC, each step changes one character and each result is in the bank

optimal.time: O(b * L * 4) where b is bank size and L is gene length (8), since each BFS step tries changing each of L positions to each of 4 letters and checks bank membership
optimal.space: O(b) for the bank set and visited set
optimal.pattern: BFS shortest path over an implicit graph where nodes are genes and edges connect genes that differ by exactly one character, restricted to genes present in the bank

bruteForce.approach: explore every possible sequence of mutations from startGene via DFS/backtracking, trying all valid single-character changes at each step and checking membership in the bank, tracking the best (shortest) sequence found
bruteForce.time: O(4^L * b) in the worst case, where L is gene length and b is bank size, due to redundant re-exploration of the same states
